map.骨折后出血形成血肿，逐渐机化形成纤维连接。此期需固定制动，避免移位。: Bleeding after fracture forms a hematoma that gradually organizes into a fibrous connection. This stage needs immobilization to avoid displacement.
map.软骨痂逐渐骨化为原始骨痂，X线可见骨痂影。此期可开始轻度功能锻炼。: The cartilaginous callus gradually ossifies into primary callus, visible on X-ray. Light functional exercise can start in this stage.
map.原始骨痂逐渐改造为成熟骨小梁，强度增加。可逐渐恢复正常活动。: The primary callus gradually remodels into mature trabeculae, increasing strength. Normal activity can be gradually resumed.
map.骨结构按力学要求重塑，最终恢复接近正常形态。儿童塑形能力强于成人。: Bone structure remodels per mechanical demand and finally recovers near-normal shape. Children's modeling ability is stronger than adults'.

map.场景：以常见四肢骨折为例，按部位与年龄查表。\n桡骨远端骨折：儿童 3–5 周、:
Scenario: take common limb fractures as an example, look up by body part and age. 
 Distal radius fracture: child 3-5 weeks, youth 6-8 weeks, middle age 8-10 weeks, elderly 10-12 weeks for clinical union; light activity after 4-6 weeks. 
 Femoral shaft fracture: youth 8-12 weeks, elderly 12-20 weeks; often needs internal fixation, gradual weight-bearing after 8-12 weeks. 
 Femoral neck fracture: often needs surgery; early mobilization after internal fixation or arthroplasty, bony union about 12-16 weeks. 
 Conclusion: for the same fracture, the older the age the slower the healing (elderly about 1.3-1.7x the youth); and 'can move' is far earlier than 'can fully bear weight'.
map.为什么医生说「长好了」但还不能负重？: Why does the doctor say 'healed' but you still cannot bear weight?
map.骨折愈合分纤维愈合、临床愈合与骨性愈合三阶段。临床愈合（压痛消失、X 线连续骨痂: Fracture healing has three stages: fibrous union, clinical union and bony union. Clinical union (no tenderness, continuous callus on X-ray) allows removing the cast for light activity, but reaching bony strength for full weight-bearing often needs several more weeks. Follow medical advice step by step; premature loading easily deforms or re-fractures.
map.吃什么能加速骨折愈合？: What to eat to speed fracture healing?
map.愈合主要靠自身成骨与稳定固定，营养是基础而非「特效药」。保证充足蛋白质、钙、维生: Healing mainly relies on the body's own osteogenesis and stable fixation; nutrition is a base, not a 'magic bullet'. Ensure adequate protein, calcium, vitamin D and moderate sun exposure; quit smoking (nicotine clearly inhibits osteogenesis). This table is a time reference; actual follow-up imaging is the standard—do not load early by feel.
